FEA-CH-32.text:
The five kinds stay, anchored to data and placed by the shared label search, and the set grows into hand-made annotations: an author's own marks, written in the source and drawn in the style's own strokes, in pencil only in Hand-drawn (Daniel, 23 November 2026).

- **The set.** A note at a point, a circled set of points with a note, a bracket between two values, horizontal and vertical lines, shaded ranges and free text. No boxed callouts.
- **Anchors are data, never positions.** An anchor is x and y, x and a series, a set of points, or one value. A mark stays with its data when the reader filters, zooms or plays, and leaves the view with it.
- **Notes stand at their marks.** The engine places a note; the author may name a side as a hint, never an offset. An arrow or leader is the engine's fallback for a note that does not fit beside its mark, not something an author asks for. A note with no room wraps beside its mark, then stands off on a leader, and only then is left out and reported (FEA-CH-29). There is no numbered key under the chart.
- **The bracket's number is computed** by RichView from the rows of the reader's current state, as a difference, a percent change or a compound growth rate, in the chart's number format and at the author's precision (FEA-CH-37). The author's text is an optional label beside it.
- **Lines are solid**, in a grey of the style, with the label at the side. Today's dashed lines are reworked.
- **Out:** positions in pixels or as a share of the plot; freehand strokes, icons and images on the plot; the pencil look outside Hand-drawn; a colour or stroke chosen per annotation; and placing marks with the pointer in the editor, which may come later and write the same source.
- **Guidance for authors and agents:** an event tied to an x value is a vertical line; a ring is for a point that is itself the subject.

The first build covers line, area, bar and scatter charts; other chart types warn that they draw no annotations yet. The field names for the circle, the bracket, the series anchor and the side hint belong to TYP-19, whose proposal follows this answer. Hand-drawn's pencil for rings and leaders stays as STY-35 proposes. Annotations fade in with the labels after the marks, as proposed. The benchmark Daniel named is a PowerPoint chart add-in with annotations, read as think-cell.

FEA-CH-37.text:
Numbers follow a three-digit rule by default: at most three significant digits, four at most, with a scale word, for example 1.23 million, 167.5 thousand or 167 thousand.

Readers never get more precision than the author chose to show. Readouts, tooltips, the Table view, CSV and every export show values at the author's chosen precision; the underlying, more exact source values cannot be retrieved. Otherwise what a reader can dig out would differ from what the author and reviewers saw, and could disclose how precise the author's calculations are.

The author can set more or fewer digits, per chart or per element, and can give tooltips a higher precision than labels; readers then see that precision, and no more. There is no warning at publish time.
FEA-CH-37.note: Dictated by Daniel in the review chat on 2026-10-26: "The three-digit system I had: three digits, at max four, so you can have 1.23 million or 167.5 thousand, or just 167 thousand. If you want to see a table, there should be a way to explore the value that the author decided to put in. By default you should not be able to retrieve the underlying ultra-exact values, because that could show a difference between what the author and reviewer see at first level and could disclose things they don't want disclosed, like how precise their calculations are. The author needs to be able to set more or fewer digits, for example tooltip precision higher than the normal precision. Getting to the underlying data shouldn't give you more detail than the first way you see it. No warning when publishing." Recorded by the lockdown agent at his request.
